notes: Canonical variable codebook. Updated for Draft 0.5: (1) scope expanded from 3 to 5 concepts (added Care, Loyalty); (2) parameter codes updated — PLB→LL, CAT→RT, SMG→MS; (3) parameter 10 replaced: TO (Temporal Orientation) dropped, AW (Affective Weighting) added; (4) configurations expanded from 2³=8 to 2⁵=32. Parameter order in R: [LL, CS, RT, MoR, RE, PD, TfA, ID, MS, AW]. Verified PSD: min eigenvalue = 0.311.

variables.name: LL
variables.label: Legitimacy Locus
variables.endpoint_0: validity depends on internal endorsement, personal judgment, or self-authentication
variables.endpoint_1: validity depends on external recognition, shared norms, role structure, or institutional warrant
variables.proxy_instrument: General Causality Orientations Scale (GCOS; Deci & Ryan, 1985)
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing after sampling
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(3.5, 2.5) via Gaussian copula marginal
variables.cross_concept_role: Freedom: is agency validated internally or by recognised conditions? Justice: are fairness judgments personal-intuitive or norm-anchored? Authority: is obedience earned by office, expertise, or shared norm? Care: does compassion extend on personal grounds or by institutional deservingness? Loyalty: are group bonds sustained by internal commitment or external markers?
variables.notes: LL ↔ ID correlation (r=0.45) is the strongest in R, anchored in SDT motivational framework.

variables.name: CS
variables.label: Constraint Sensitivity
variables.endpoint_0: low sensitivity; influence and structure registered as neutral environmental features
variables.endpoint_1: high sensitivity; even soft nudges register as potential constraints
variables.proxy_instrument: Hong Psychological Reactance Scale (HPRS; Hong & Faedda, 1996)
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.5, 2.0) via Gaussian copula marginal
variables.cross_concept_role: Central to freedom (constraint detection). Determines how readily injustice is detected, whether authority is experienced as coercive, whether help is received as paternalism, whether in-group expectations feel like identity-coercion.
variables.notes: CS ↔ TfA (r=−0.35): high reactance predicts rejection of asymmetric arrangements. CS ↔ RE (r=−0.30): individualists experience stronger personal-freedom threats. CS ↔ MoR (r=0.30).

variables.name: RT
variables.label: Response Threshold
variables.endpoint_0: high tolerance; responds only to major violations
variables.endpoint_1: low tolerance; activated by mild deviations
variables.proxy_instrument: Ultimatum Game rejection thresholds (Wallace et al., 2007; meta-analysis of 37 papers)
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.5, 2.5) via Gaussian copula marginal
variables.cross_concept_role: Determines when constraint triggers resistance (freedom), when inequity triggers correction (justice), when illegitimate command triggers refusal (authority), when suffering activates helping (care), when group-threat activates protective action (loyalty).
variables.notes: RT ↔ MS (r=0.35): agents with broader moral scope tend to have lower tolerance for moral deviation. RT ↔ TfA (r=−0.30): agents who accept asymmetry tolerate more violation before responding.

variables.name: MoR
variables.label: Mode of Response
variables.endpoint_0: internal, reflective, self-adjusting; the self adjusts rather than the world
variables.endpoint_1: external, behavioural, confrontational; the world is acted on rather than the self
variables.proxy_instrument: STAXI (Spielberger, 1988) Anger-In/Out ratio; Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument; Davis IRI Empathic Concern vs. Personal Distress distinction
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.0, 2.5) via Gaussian copula marginal
variables.cross_concept_role: Bridges the parameter layer to observable behaviour across all five concepts. Determines whether activation produces internal adjustment or external confrontation.
variables.notes: Avoiding and accommodating styles more common than competing/confronting in general Western populations.

variables.name: RE
variables.label: Relational Embedding
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.0, 3.0) via Gaussian copula marginal. Italian sub-calibration: Beta(2.5, 3.0).
variables.cross_concept_role: Foundational for loyalty (loyalty presupposes relational embedding). Load-bearing for care through the universalist-vs-partialist distinction (Bloom 2016; Greene 2013). Modulates whether standards applied uniformly or contextually by relationship.
variables.notes: CS ↔ RE (r=−0.30): independent self-construal positively correlates with personal reactance.

variables.name: PD
variables.label: Procedural Dependence
variables.endpoint_0: outcome-dominant; results matter, methods are secondary
variables.endpoint_1: process-dominant; fair procedure matters independently of outcomes
variables.proxy_instrument: Colquitt (2001) Organisational Justice Scale; trolley-problem response data
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.5, 2.0) via Gaussian copula marginal
variables.cross_concept_role: Authority legitimacy depends heavily on mandate, due process, and consent. Loyalty can be enacted through ritual form (Whitehouse 2018) or substantive support. Empirically separable from distributive justice.
variables.notes: Western populations split ~60/40 consequentialist over deontological. Distributive concerns slightly stronger predictors of workplace satisfaction.

variables.name: TfA
variables.label: Tolerance for Asymmetry
variables.endpoint_0: asymmetry is inherently suspect, requiring justification; default expectation is symmetry
variables.endpoint_1: asymmetry is accepted if intelligible or justified; default accommodates hierarchy
variables.proxy_instrument: Social Dominance Orientation (SDO7; Pratto et al., 1994; Ho et al., 2015)
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.0, 3.5) via Gaussian copula marginal. Mixture fallback if bimodality confirmed: 0.6×Beta(2,4) + 0.4×Beta(4,2).
variables.cross_concept_role: Best empirically anchored parameter. US mean SDO = 2.98/7 ≈ 0.43, NZ study 91% in low-to-moderate range.
variables.notes: TfA ↔ MS (r=−0.40): strongest negative in R. SDO correlates at r≈−0.42 with MFQ individualising foundations.

variables.name: ID
variables.label: Internalisation Dependence
variables.endpoint_0: can operate through compliance, sanctions, and surface behaviour alone
variables.endpoint_1: requires genuine belief, endorsement, or value-congruence
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(3.0, 2.0) via Gaussian copula marginal
variables.cross_concept_role: Directly operationalises Kelman's compliance–identification–internalisation ladder. Connects all five concept definitions at the deepest level.
variables.notes: LL ↔ ID (r=0.45) is the strongest correlation in R. Renamed from PLB to LL in Draft 0.5.

variables.name: MS
variables.label: Moral Scope
variables.formerly: SMG (Scope of Moral Generalisation) — renamed Draft 0.5. MFQ-only anchor replaced by MES as primary.
variables.proxy_instrument: Moral Expansiveness Scale (MES; Crimston et al. 2016; MESx short-form 2018). Secondary: IWAH (McFarland et al. 2012).
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(1.8, 1.5) via Gaussian copula marginal. Mixture fallback if bimodality confirmed: 0.55×Beta(3,1.5) + 0.45×Beta(1.5,3).
variables.cross_concept_role: MES is the direct instrument for expanding-circle operationalisation. Load-bearing for care (who is cared for) and loyalty (how wide the loyalty target). In productive tension with TfA.
variables.notes: Primary anchor changed from MFQ-2 to MES in Draft 0.5. Liberal/conservative split may produce genuine bimodality.

variables.name: AW
variables.label: Affective Weighting
variables.formerly: NEW in Draft 0.5. Replaces TO (Temporal Orientation) which was dropped.
variables.proxy_instrument: Davis IRI — Empathic Concern vs. Perspective Taking subscale ratio (Davis, 1983). Supporting: Greene et al. (2001) dual-process moral judgment; Haidt (2001) social intuitionist model.
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Sampled from Beta(2.2, 2.5) via Gaussian copula marginal. Beta calibration is PRELIMINARY — to be refined against IRI population norms once implementation is underway.
variables.cross_concept_role: Cuts across all five concepts: felt autonomy vs. reasoned autonomy, moral outrage vs. equity calculation, charismatic vs. rational-legal authority, empathic concern vs. reasoned beneficence, identity fusion vs. deliberated commitment.
variables.notes: Newly introduced in Draft 0.5. AW row in R contains theoretically motivated correlations rather than direct empirical ones — explicit targets for sensitivity analysis and empirical refinement.

variables.name: societal_freedom
variables.label: Societal Freedom Level
variables.endpoint_0: Low-Freedom: constrained choice, structured expectations, limited exit options, penalties for deviation
variables.endpoint_1: High-Freedom: protected individual choice, exit options, informational access, low deviation penalties
variables.missing_meaning: Configuration not set — simulation cannot run
variables.transformation: Set at simulation initialisation, not sampled
variables.notes: Bit 1 of config_code (5-bit string, leftmost).

variables.name: societal_justice
variables.label: Societal Justice Level
variables.endpoint_0: Low-Justice: distribution follows power/precedent, no formal complaint mechanisms, no transparency
variables.endpoint_1: High-Justice: transparent allocation rules, proportionality and procedural fairness enforced, complaint mechanisms exist
variables.missing_meaning: Configuration not set — simulation cannot run
variables.transformation: Set at simulation initialisation, not sampled
variables.notes: Bit 2 of config_code.

variables.name: societal_authority
variables.label: Societal Authority Level
variables.endpoint_0: Low-Authority: horizontal coordination, no role-based directive power, voluntary association
variables.endpoint_1: High-Authority: directive power vested in roles, chains of command exist, disobedience is costly
variables.missing_meaning: Configuration not set — simulation cannot run
variables.transformation: Set at simulation initialisation, not sampled
variables.notes: Bit 3 of config_code.

variables.name: societal_care
variables.label: Societal Care Level
variables.endpoint_0: Low-Care: no systematic protection of vulnerable members, welfare falls to private action or chance
variables.endpoint_1: High-Care: structural supports for vulnerable members — welfare, health, safety nets — norms of concern enforced
variables.missing_meaning: Configuration not set — simulation cannot run
variables.transformation: Set at simulation initialisation, not sampled
variables.notes: Bit 4 of config_code. NEW in Draft 0.5.

variables.name: societal_loyalty
variables.label: Societal Loyalty Level
variables.endpoint_0: Low-Loyalty: memberships are instrumental, exit is unconstrained, no cost for group defection
variables.endpoint_1: High-Loyalty: demonstrated loyalty rewarded, costs imposed for defection, group boundaries marked and enforced
variables.missing_meaning: Configuration not set — simulation cannot run
variables.transformation: Set at simulation initialisation, not sampled
variables.notes: Bit 5 of config_code (rightmost). NEW in Draft 0.5.

variables.name: config_code
variables.label: Societal Configuration Code
variables.missing_meaning: Configuration not set — error
variables.transformation: Derived from (societal_freedom, societal_justice, societal_authority, societal_care, societal_loyalty)
variables.notes: Draft 0.5: expanded from 3-bit (8 configs) to 5-bit (32 configs). Proof-of-concept tests a defensible subset of 8–12 spanning the most antagonistic combinations. Milgram-analogue config: 00100 (F=0, J=0, A=1, C=0, L=0).

variables.name: obedience_rate
variables.label: Obedience Rate
variables.missing_meaning: Simulation run did not complete
variables.transformation: Computed as: (agents fully complying with authority directive) / (total agents). Definition of 'fully complying' is TBD — see Open Problem L1 in meta.md.
variables.notes: PRIMARY VALIDATION METRIC for Authority. Config 00100 must produce 0.61–0.66 to pass Milgram retrodiction. Report as point estimate with 95% CI across simulation runs.

variables.name: welfare_score
variables.label: Composite Welfare Score
variables.missing_meaning: Not yet computable — performance metric undefined
variables.transformation: NOT YET DEFINED. Open Problem L1 in meta.md. Do not implement a proxy without panel review and human sign-off.
variables.notes: CRITICAL OPEN PROBLEM. Do not operationalise this without explicit approval.

variables.name: agent_id
variables.label: Agent Unique Identifier
variables.missing_meaning: Sampling bug — should never be missing
variables.transformation: Assigned at agent creation: format '{config_code}_{run_id}_{agent_index}'
variables.notes: Unique within a run, not across runs.

variables.name: run_id
variables.label: Simulation Run Identifier
variables.missing_meaning: Run not logged — error
variables.transformation: Format: '{config_code}_{YYYYMMDD}_{run_index}_{seed}'
variables.notes: Always log the random seed. Reproducibility requires seed tracking.

variables.name: random_seed
variables.label: Random Seed
variables.missing_meaning: Run not reproducible — error
variables.transformation: Set before any NumPy/OpenAI API call. Logged to output/logs/pipeline.log.
variables.notes: Every simulation result must report its seed. No unreproducible runs.

correlation_matrix_R.description: 10×10 Gaussian copula correlation matrix R. Parameter order: [LL, CS, RT, MoR, RE, PD, TfA, ID, MS, AW]. Defined and instantiated in code/utils.py. Verified PSD: min eigenvalue = 0.311. Do not modify R entries without panel review and eigendecomposition re-verification.

sensitivity_regimes.regime_a: R as specified in methods paper §3.4.4 (baseline)
sensitivity_regimes.regime_b: R with all |r| < 0.25 set to zero (strongly anchored correlations only)
sensitivity_regimes.regime_c: R with all correlations inflated by 20% — re-verify PSD before use via Higham (2002) if non-PSD

correlation_matrix_R.AW_note: AW row contains theoretically motivated correlations rather than directly empirical ones. Explicit targets for sensitivity analysis and empirical refinement once AW is operationalised against IRI population data.
